output.reason: The changelog line on its own is vague [ev-522e37356d1b], but the linked PR makes it concrete. It names the subject and the change: two new LogQL line filter operators, `|>` and `!>`, that match lines against a pattern. They use the same semantics as the `pattern` parse stage, except that named captures are not allowed, and `"<_>"` matches any non-empty line [ev-96b69e204b54]. The PR describes this as an explicit addition to the query syntax that is experimental and undocumented [ev-62573bd7c853], and the changed files are confined to the LogQL parser, lexer and filter code plus a bloom tester [ev-59e75069cc60]. That is enough to write the open applicability aspect: only queries that opt in by using `|>` or `!>` are exposed, and existing queries do nothing that would expose them.
